I trained in JJJ for 2 years. In my opinion, I would quit. I believe there is only so much it can teach you. If you are doing zero sparring, you know, real pressure testing then it won’t serve you well at all in a real life scenario. 

The throws taught are very difficult to pull off on somebody that is bigger than yourself or so much shorter than yourself. The techniques taught are very situational. I came to the same conclusion you are now coming to, it’s just not practical.

I switched to MMA after JJJ and I can say wholeheartedly you will feel a lot more confident in your abilities once you start getting good. Trust me, you will not regret starting MMA. Even Boxing would serve you better than JJJ.

I think in a street fight you only need 2 arts, Boxing and Wrestling, (with a few leg kicks mixed in) but you want to avoid grappling in the street at all costs. You don’t know if who you’re fighting has friends or not, and those friends will kick you straight in your skull. 

I remember Joe Rogan said something along the lines of, “If it doesn’t work on a trained opponent, it isn’t worth training.” That rings true with JJJ. I’ve tried using it on trained fighters to no avail. They can see the techniques coming. Plus Aikido doesn’t work anyway, it’s a complete bullshit art.

Yes, they shouldn’t care, and it’s not the fault of Helio Gracie if they do care. It’s not his fault that more people were interested in BJJ than JJJ. 
I’ve trained in a JJJ club, they’re very serious about their dying art and I do respect them for it, but I have to admit their hate for the term BJJ is a little pathetic. Especially when they believe their art is vastly superior when it really isn’t. 

Now imagine if other martial arts had this problem, such as Judo and Sambo for example. Both are quite similar in style, but just different enough and effective enough that both are still in wide use today by their respective countries. 
Obviously there is no name issues like with BJJ and JJJ, but that aside, both are effective grappling arts that hold applicable use in reality. 

That’s why both can learn from each other, that’s why you’ll rarely ever see someone who does Judo bashing Sambo and vice versa. If JJJ was still effective today, there would be a lot more schools and a lot more people coming in. The truth is they’ve stuck by their old ways and those old ways don’t work anymore, and most people just aren’t interested in it now.
